subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 0 easy / 100 medium / 0 hard. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: True leg length is measured from the:

options.B: Anterior superior iliac spine to the medial malleolus
options.C: Greater trochanter to the lateral malleolus

questions.explanation: True length: ASIS to medial malleolus; apparent length: umbilicus (or xiphisternum) to the medial malleolus.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Massage is contraindicated over:

options.A: A deep vein thrombosis, acute inflammation or malignancy

questions.explanation: Massage may dislodge thrombus or spread infection and tumour cells.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: In a boutonnière deformity of the finger the typical posture is:

options.D: Ulnar deviation at the MCP only

questions.explanation: Central slip rupture lets the lateral bands slip volar to the PIP axis: PIP flexes and DIP hyperextends. A swan-neck is the reverse (PIP hyperextension, DIP flexion).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Dark urine and pale stools with jaundice suggest:
questions.explanation: Conjugated bilirubin is excreted in urine; no stercobilin reaches the gut.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Which autoantibody is characteristic of Hashimoto's thyroiditis?
questions.explanation: Anti-dsDNA is characteristic of SLE.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Gestational diabetes mellitus is screened for with a glucose tolerance test at:
questions.explanation: Risks: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, neonatal hypoglycaemia.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Which muscle prevents winging of the scapula?
questions.explanation: Serratus anterior holds the scapula against the thoracic wall.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Erythema after UVB exposure is mainly due to:

options.B: Release of vasodilator chemicals (histamine-like substances, prostaglandins) from damaged epidermal cells

questions.explanation: UV damages keratinocytes, releasing vasoactive substances that dilate dermal capillaries after a latent period (hours).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A combination of upper and lower motor neurone signs without sensory loss is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: ALS: wasting and fasciculations (LMN) with spasticity and hyperreflexia (UMN); sensation and eye movements are preserved.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Which structure is NOT commonly associated with posterior dislocation of the elbow?
questions.explanation: Myositis ossificans traumatica (not progressiva) can complicate an elbow injury.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The SAID principle (Specific Adaptation to Imposed Demands) means that:

options.B: The body adapts specifically to the type of exercise (mode, speed, range) it performs
options.C: Strength gains transfer equally to all movements

questions.explanation: Training should replicate functional demands in contraction type, velocity and joint angle.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The most specific antibody for systemic lupus erythematosus is:
questions.explanation: ANA is sensitive but not specific; butterfly rash, arthritis, nephritis.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Aerobic training mainly improves:

options.C: Maximal oxygen uptake (VO2 max) and cardiovascular endurance

questions.explanation: Training adaptations include increased stroke volume, capillary density and mitochondrial enzymes.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: A warning sign of severe dengue is:

options.A: Abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, mucosal bleeding and a rapid fall in platelet count

questions.explanation: Plasma leakage causes shock; monitor haematocrit and platelets.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The Gross Motor Function Classification System (GMFCS) for cerebral palsy has:

options.A: Five levels, I being the least impaired and V the most

questions.explanation: Level I walks without limitations; level V is transported in a manual wheelchair.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The energy value of one gram of fat is:
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate 4, protein 4, fat 9, alcohol 7 kcal per gram.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The anterior drawer test of the ankle stresses the:
questions.explanation: Anterior translation of the talus from the mortise indicates ATFL laxity.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Gas gangrene is caused by:
questions.explanation: Characterised by crepitus, foul-smelling discharge and rapid spreading myonecrosis; treated by radical debridement and penicillin.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Klumpke's paralysis involves the:

options.D: Lower trunk (C8–T1), causing paralysis of the intrinsic hand muscles

questions.explanation: Klumpke's palsy affects C8–T1: claw hand with possible Horner's syndrome if T1 sympathetic fibres are involved.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Resisted isometric movement that is strong and painful suggests a lesion of:
questions.explanation: Cyriax: pain on resisted testing with full passive range indicates a contractile lesion; painful passive and active movement (non-contractile) suggests an inert structure.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 in India recognises how many categories of disability?
questions.explanation: It increased the number from 7 (PwD Act 1995) to 21 benchmark categories and ensures 4% reservation in government jobs.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over about:
questions.explanation: Reflects glycation of haemoglobin over the 120-day red cell lifespan.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Before exercising, a person with type 1 diabetes should check blood glucose and avoid exercise if:

options.B: Glucose is very low, or high with ketones present

questions.explanation: Hypoglycaemia and ketosis are risks; carry fast-acting carbohydrate and monitor glucose.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: In the ICIDH model, difficulty in performing an activity such as walking due to an impairment is termed:
questions.explanation: Impairment (organ level) → disability (person level) → handicap (social level).
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: A true interference pattern (endogenous IFT) in the tissues requires:

options.A: A quadripolar electrode arrangement with the two circuits crossing at the target
options.C: A single large and small electrode
options.D: A bipolar arrangement with premodulated current

questions.explanation: In quadripolar technique two separate circuits cross; the interference occurs within the tissue. In bipolar mode the current is premodulated within the machine, so no true interference occurs in the tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The original Borg Rating of Perceived Exertion scale runs from:
questions.explanation: The 6–20 scale approximates heart rate/10; the modified CR10 scale runs 0–10. A rating of 12–14 is typical for moderate exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Vitamin C is required for:

options.D: Hydroxylation of proline and lysine in collagen synthesis

questions.explanation: Deficiency causes scurvy with bleeding gums and poor wound healing.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: A fracture of the shaft of the humerus most commonly injures the:
questions.explanation: In the spiral groove.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: A Bankart lesion is:

options.A: A compression defect of the posterolateral humeral head
options.B: Avulsion of the anteroinferior glenoid labrum with the capsule
options.D: A tear of the long head of biceps

questions.explanation: Anterior dislocation avulses the anteroinferior labrum (Bankart); the humeral head impacts to cause a Hill–Sachs defect posterolaterally.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which tissue has the LOWEST thermal conductivity and so insulates the underlying tissues from superficial heat?
questions.explanation: Fat is a poor conductor; heat applied to a thick fatty layer penetrates less, and is retained within the fat, increasing the risk of superficial burns.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Cortisol secretion shows a diurnal rhythm with the peak at:
questions.explanation: It increases blood glucose, suppresses inflammation and mobilises protein.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: The most important factor maintaining stability of the shoulder joint is the:
questions.explanation: The shallow glenoid and loose capsule favour mobility at the expense of stability.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Which of these is a classic feature of a panic attack, as distinguished from generalised anxiety?

options.A: Gradual worsening of mild anxiety over several months
options.B: A sudden, discrete episode of severe anxiety, often beginning unexpectedly 'out of the blue' and lasting only a few minutes
options.C: Anxiety present continuously for years without any discrete episodes
options.D: Anxiety that only occurs during sleep

questions.explanation: Panic disorder is characterised by discrete episodes of acute, severe anxiety that begin suddenly, often 'out of the blue' with no apparent precipitant, and last for a few minutes — quite different from the more continuous, lower-grade anxiety of generalised anxiety disorder.
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.sourceChapter: Neurotic, Stress-related and Somatoform Disorders — Anxiety Disorder
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: Van't Hoff's law relates to the therapeutic effect of heat by stating that:

options.A: The rate of a chemical reaction (metabolic rate) increases about two to three times for each 10 °C rise in temperature
options.C: Absorbed radiation produces a chemical change only when it penetrates
options.D: Heat produced is proportional to current squared

questions.explanation: Van't Hoff's law underlies the increase in tissue metabolism with heating, which increases demand for oxygen and promotes repair.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Phonophoresis is the use of ultrasound to:

options.A: Reduce skin resistance to direct current
options.B: Drive a topical drug through the skin into underlying tissue
options.C: Remove a drug from the blood

questions.explanation: Phonophoresis uses acoustic streaming and increased membrane permeability to deliver topical agents such as hydrocortisone or NSAIDs.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Broca's (expressive) aphasia is characterised by:

options.C: Fluent but meaningless speech with poor comprehension

questions.explanation: Lesion of the inferior frontal gyrus (dominant hemisphere). In Wernicke's aphasia speech is fluent but nonsensical with impaired comprehension.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The highest level of complete spinal cord injury at which a patient can be expected to feed themselves with a long opponens splint and adaptive devices is:
questions.explanation: At C5 biceps and deltoid are functional so feeding with devices is possible; C6 adds wrist extension; C7 triceps allows independent transfers.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Spurling's test (neck extension, side-flexion with axial compression) is used to detect:
questions.explanation: Reduction of the intervertebral foramen reproduces arm pain in nerve root compression.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The cardinal features of intestinal obstruction are:

options.C: Colicky pain, vomiting, distension and absolute constipation

questions.explanation: Adhesions and hernias are the commonest causes of small bowel obstruction.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Poliomyelitis causes paralysis through destruction of:
questions.explanation: Flaccid, asymmetric paralysis with preserved sensation; post-polio syndrome appears decades later.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: In a young woman a firm, smooth, mobile, painless breast lump is most likely a:
questions.explanation: Fibroadenoma is called a ‘breast mouse’ due to its mobility.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Anterior pelvic tilt increases:
questions.explanation: Tight hip flexors and weak abdominals increase anterior pelvic tilt.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The active cycle of breathing technique (ACBT) consists of:

options.D: Breathing control, thoracic expansion exercises and the forced expiration technique

questions.explanation: ACBT cycles include breathing control (relaxed tidal breathing), deep breathing exercises and huffing (FET), repeated until the chest is clear.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The normal range of ankle dorsiflexion is about:
questions.explanation: AAOS: ankle dorsiflexion 0–20°, plantar flexion 0–50°, inversion 0–35°, eversion 0–15°.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Despite his severe memory problems, patient H.M. had relatively normal short-term memory (e.g. could repeat six numbers forward after hearing them once) and intact memories from before his operation. What was specifically impaired?

options.A: His ability to form new long-term memories
options.B: His personality and IQ, both of which dropped sharply
options.C: His sense of touch and vision
options.D: His ability to speak or understand language

questions.explanation: H.M.'s deficit was specifically in forming new long-term memories (anterograde amnesia) — his immediate/short-term memory and his remote memories from before the surgery were largely preserved, illustrating that short-term and long-term memory, and the process of consolidating one into the other, are at least partly separable.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Biology of Behavior — Temporal-Lobe Association Cortex, Memory Functions
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: A positive Romberg test (swaying or falling with the eyes closed) indicates loss of:
questions.explanation: Standing with feet together and eyes closed removes visual compensation; sway indicates a sensory ataxia.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: If a patient's active range is less than passive range at the knee, the most likely cause is:
questions.explanation: When PROM is greater than AROM the limitation is in the contractile unit; when both are equally limited the joint structures are restricted.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: A 14-year-old girl has a 25° thoracic scoliosis. The appropriate initial management is:

options.B: Observation or bracing with exercises, not surgery

questions.explanation: Curves < 25° are observed; 25–45° in a growing child are braced (Boston/Milwaukee); > 45–50° may need surgery.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Cryotherapy is used to temporarily reduce spasticity because it:

options.B: Lowers nerve conduction velocity and muscle spindle firing

questions.explanation: Cooling decreases afferent firing and conduction velocity, lowering tone for a short period during which stretching or exercise can be performed.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In the standard manual muscle test for the gluteus medius the patient lies:

options.A: Supine with the hip flexed to 90°
options.C: On the side with the test leg uppermost, abducting in slight extension and lateral rotation neutral
options.D: Prone with the knee flexed to 90°

questions.explanation: Side-lying with the hip slightly extended and neutral rotation to avoid substitution by TFL (flexion/medial rotation) and the hip flexors.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Decorticate rigidity consists of:

options.D: Flexion of the upper limbs with extension of the lower limbs

questions.explanation: Decorticate = lesion above the red nucleus (arms flexed); decerebrate = extension and pronation of arms with extension of legs (brainstem lesion).
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The temporomandibular joint most commonly dislocates:

options.C: Anteriorly, as the condyle moves in front of the articular eminence

questions.explanation: Yawning, seizures or dental procedures can precipitate it.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: For pain relief through the gate-control mechanism, the beat frequency of IFT is usually set at about:
questions.explanation: High beat frequencies (~80–100 Hz) favour the segmental gate mechanism; low frequencies (2–10 Hz) favour endorphin-mediated pain relief and muscle contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Propranolol is contraindicated in:
questions.explanation: Non-selective beta-blockade causes bronchoconstriction; also contraindicated in heart block.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: Which is a major criterion in the Jones criteria for rheumatic fever?

options.B: Carditis, migratory polyarthritis, chorea, erythema marginatum and subcutaneous nodules

questions.explanation: Minor criteria: fever, arthralgia, raised acute phase reactants, prolonged PR interval.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Compared with non-luminous infrared generators, luminous generators:

options.C: Emit longer wavelengths absorbed in the outer epidermis only
options.D: Emit shorter-wavelength IR that penetrates a little deeper, along with visible light, and need no warm-up

questions.explanation: Luminous IR lamps (filament lamps) emit visible and near-IR radiation (to ~ 5–10 mm); non-luminous generators use heated elements, emit longer wavelengths absorbed superficially and require 5–10 minutes to warm up.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Over a large pleural effusion, the percussion note is:
questions.explanation: Dullness with reduced/absent breath sounds and reduced vocal resonance; hyper-resonance occurs in pneumothorax.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which is NOT a radiological feature of osteoarthritis?
questions.explanation: OA features: narrowing of joint space, osteophytes, sclerosis, cysts. Widening is not a feature.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: In PNF, the technique that uses an isometric contraction of the antagonist (tight) muscle followed by relaxation and passive movement into increased range is:
questions.explanation: Hold–relax and contract–relax technique improve range by autogenic inhibition; agonist contraction techniques use reciprocal inhibition.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: One MET is approximately equal to an oxygen consumption of:
questions.explanation: 1 MET = resting oxygen consumption (3.5 mL O2 per kg per minute). Light activity 1.6–3 METs, moderate 3–6, vigorous >6.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The first-line drug for generalised tonic–clonic seizures is:

options.B: Phenobarbitone in adults as first choice

questions.explanation: Carbamazepine is for focal seizures; ethosuximide for absence.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: In established Volkmann's ischaemic contracture, the finger deformity is reduced (fingers can be extended) when the wrist is:
questions.explanation: Flexor muscles are shortened; flexing the wrist slackens them and allows the fingers to straighten. With the wrist extended the fingers flex (tenodesis effect).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Paraplegia in spinal tuberculosis is most common when the disease is in the:
questions.explanation: The thoracic canal is narrowest relative to the cord and a kyphotic angulation easily compresses it; early signs include flexor spasms and exaggerated reflexes.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The clavicle is unique because it:

options.A: Is a long bone with a medullary canal
options.B: Ossifies in membrane and also has a cartilaginous growth centre at its ends
options.C: Is the last bone to ossify

questions.explanation: It begins ossifying around the 5th–6th week of intrauterine life, the first bone to ossify.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: A granuloma is a collection of:

options.D: Activated macrophages (epithelioid cells), often with giant cells and lymphocytes

questions.explanation: Seen in TB, sarcoidosis, leprosy and Crohn's disease.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: To allow adaptation, resistance exercise for the same muscle group is generally performed:

options.D: 2–3 times per week with at least 48 hours between sessions

questions.explanation: Muscle adapts during recovery; ACSM recommends 2–3 days per week for each major muscle group.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Flexion of the elbow by the biceps with a weight in the hand is an example of a:
questions.explanation: The muscle effort acts between the axis (elbow) and the resistance (weight in the hand).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: In Paget's disease of bone the serum alkaline phosphatase is typically:
questions.explanation: Also bone pain, deformity (sabre tibia), deafness and risk of osteosarcoma.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The artery most commonly involved in anterior wall myocardial infarction is the:
questions.explanation: The ‘widow-maker’ supplies the anterior LV wall and interventricular septum.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Dry gangrene is typically caused by:

options.D: Arterial occlusion, as in diabetes or atherosclerosis

questions.explanation: Wet gangrene has superadded infection with putrefaction.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Head-down postural drainage should be avoided in patients with:

options.A: Raised intracranial pressure, uncontrolled hypertension or acute heart failure

questions.explanation: Head-down tilt increases venous return and intracranial pressure and may precipitate pulmonary oedema or reflux/aspiration.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: In a muscle immobilised in a shortened position the typical adaptation is:

options.D: Loss of sarcomeres in series, so the muscle becomes shorter

questions.explanation: Muscles adapt to their functional length; immobilised in lengthened position they add sarcomeres.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Risk factors for uterovaginal prolapse include:

options.B: Multiparity, obesity, chronic cough and menopause

questions.explanation: Pelvic floor exercises are first-line for mild prolapse.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Which statement about collagen is correct?

options.A: Collagen fibres resist tensile forces and give tendons and ligaments strength
options.B: Collagen resists compression better than tension
options.C: Type II collagen is found mainly in tendons
options.D: Collagen is elastic and stretches by 100%

questions.explanation: Type I collagen predominates in tendons, ligaments, bone and skin; type II in hyaline cartilage.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The lateral basal segment of the right lower lobe is drained with the patient lying:

options.A: On the right side with the foot end elevated
options.D: On the left side with the foot end elevated about 20 degrees

questions.explanation: The side to be drained is uppermost; the foot of the bed is raised (head-down) to align the lower lobe bronchus with gravity.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Compared with 1 MHz ultrasound, 3 MHz ultrasound is:

options.C: Absorbed deeper and used for the hip joint
options.D: Absorbed more superficially and used for shallow structures

questions.explanation: Absorption increases with frequency; therefore 3 MHz is attenuated more rapidly and suits superficial tendons and joints.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which is NOT a ketone body?
questions.explanation: Ketone bodies are synthesised in liver mitochondria from acetyl-CoA but the liver cannot utilise them.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: The most common source of pulmonary embolism is:

options.D: Deep veins of the lower limb

questions.explanation: Deep vein thrombosis of the calf or iliofemoral veins.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: Which lamp is the best choice to irradiate a small, localised area such as a sinus or a cavity?

options.C: A water-cooled Kromayer lamp with a quartz applicator

questions.explanation: The Kromayer lamp is a water-cooled mercury vapour lamp whose UV is directed through a quartz applicator in contact with the tissue, allowing treatment of sinuses, cavities and small ulcers.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Painless recurrent vaginal bleeding in the third trimester suggests:
questions.explanation: Digital vaginal examination is contraindicated; ultrasound confirms location.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: To drain the apical segments of both upper lobes the patient is positioned:

options.B: Sitting upright, leaning slightly back or forward
options.C: Prone with the foot of the bed raised

questions.explanation: Apical bronchi are directed upward; sitting is the drainage position. Bases require head-down tilt.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Increasing the sample size in a study will generally:

options.C: Reduce the standard error and increase statistical power

questions.explanation: SE = SD/√n; larger samples give narrower confidence intervals.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The commonest pattern of diabetic peripheral neuropathy is:
questions.explanation: Chronic hyperglycaemia damages small and large fibres; foot care education is essential.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The Q-angle of the knee is formed by:

options.B: A line from the ASIS to the centre of the patella and a line from the patella to the tibial tubercle

questions.explanation: Normal Q-angle is about 13° in men and 18° in women; larger values predispose to patellar maltracking.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A grade I acromioclavicular sprain presents with:

options.B: Gross upward displacement of the clavicle
options.C: Complete rupture of the coracoclavicular ligaments
options.D: Local tenderness and mild pain, with no visible deformity and normal stability

questions.explanation: Grade I: AC ligament sprain only. Grade II: AC torn, CC sprained. Grade III: both torn with visible step deformity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The patellar apprehension test is positive in:
questions.explanation: The examiner pushes the patella laterally with the knee slightly flexed; apprehension and quadriceps contraction suggest recurrent lateral subluxation.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Vitamin K is necessary for synthesis of clotting factors:
questions.explanation: Warfarin acts by antagonising vitamin K.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Prolonged immobilisation commonly results in all EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Immobility causes disuse osteopenia, contracture, hypercalciuria with stones, pressure sores and DVT; gallstones are not an effect.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The alternating vasoconstriction and vasodilatation that occurs in the skin when cold is applied for a prolonged period is called:
questions.explanation: Prolonged cold causes cold-induced vasodilatation every few minutes to protect tissue from freezing; this limits the benefit of very long applications.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The type of rigidity in Parkinson's disease that gives a ratchet-like resistance to passive movement is called:
questions.explanation: Cogwheeling is rigidity with superimposed tremor; lead-pipe is a uniform resistance. Clasp-knife is a feature of spasticity.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: During dynamic exercise, which cardiovascular change occurs?

options.D: Increase in heart rate, stroke volume and systolic blood pressure

questions.explanation: Diastolic pressure remains unchanged or falls slightly due to vasodilatation in muscles.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: The capsular pattern of limitation of the glenohumeral joint is:
questions.explanation: Cyriax: capsular pattern at the shoulder = greatest loss of lateral rotation, then abduction, then medial rotation, as in adhesive capsulitis.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: First-pass metabolism refers to:

options.D: Metabolism of an orally absorbed drug in the liver before it reaches the systemic circulation

questions.explanation: Sublingual glyceryl trinitrate avoids first-pass effect.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: In a normal distribution, approximately what percentage of values lie within ±1 SD of the mean?
questions.explanation: 68% within ±1 SD, 95% within ±1.96 (≈2) SD, 99.7% within ±3 SD.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Which factor is MOST associated with post-operative pulmonary complications?

options.C: Upper abdominal surgery in a smoker with COPD

questions.explanation: Upper abdominal and thoracic surgery reduce diaphragm function and cough; smoking and COPD increase risk.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: A speaking valve on a tracheostomy tube may be used only if the cuff is:
questions.explanation: A one-way valve requires an open upper airway for exhalation around the tube, so cuff must be deflated.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which is NOT a subphase of the stance phase?
questions.explanation: Stance: initial contact, loading response, mid-stance, terminal stance, pre-swing. Swing: initial, mid, terminal swing.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Compared with the He–Ne laser, infrared diode lasers (e.g. 830–904 nm):
questions.explanation: Near-infrared wavelengths are absorbed less by haemoglobin and melanin, so penetrate deeper (up to a few centimetres).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: An electric-shock sensation down the spine on neck flexion (Lhermitte's sign) is classically associated with:
questions.explanation: Seen in cervical cord lesions including MS, cervical spondylosis and B12 deficiency.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) acts to:

options.C: Raise plasma calcium by increasing bone resorption and renal reabsorption and activating vitamin D

questions.explanation: Calcitonin lowers plasma calcium.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology
